hooks.name: Release Manual-Only Guard
hooks.description: PreToolUse guard on the shell tool: an agent may validate a release and commit locally, but never publish. Refuses scripts/release.sh without --dry-run, refuses --yes with or without it, refuses creating a v<semver> tag by hand, and since 2026-09-06 refuses `git push` outright — any remote, any ref, branch or tag. The push rule used to fire only on a version tag; the maintainer widened it, because deciding when work becomes visible to CI and reviewers is not the agent's call, and the narrow form also hid a matching flaw (the verb was not anchored to command position, so under a blanket ban `echo "then git push it"` would have been refused — both verbs are anchored now). --dry-run is the expected agent action on release.sh and stays allowed on push. Exists because v0.20.1 was cut by an agent with --yes and reached a pushed tag and a published GitHub release with five artifacts while carrying a red CI job and unreviewed code deletions; undoing it meant deleting a published release. `git commit`, tag listing and tag deletion stay allowed. Fails open on any internal error. Logic lives in .kiro/hooks/bin/release-manual-only-guard.sh.
